title: Absence of the Lover
text:
I have returned by the grassless path.

I go to the river in search of my shadow.

What solitude sealed by cold moon.

What solitude of water without red sirens.

What solitude of acid pines, wandering...

I go to gather up my eyes

abandoned on the shore.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the moon-sealed solitude and the abandoned eyes on the riverbank.

title: Encounter
text:
Glory of finding you!

Initial baptism of spring

in a surge of birds.


The ineffable forests moved.

Autumn undid itself of its feathers,

covering candid winters.


You were coming, gentle creature,

undressing the rivers as you passed.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the spring baptism and the beloved undressing rivers in passing.

title: Adolescence
text:
In the Dawn of her life desire

brought to her mouth the smile

on finding herself before love.


She was a girl who lived even in dreams

her ardor, and blood beat

on meeting her love.


Without the Dawn nor in the Evening

one day she asked

whether it was possible to keep

that first love of hers.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dawn/evening frame and the adolescent question of preserving first love.

title: Surrender
text:
I will keep my voice in a well of flame

and it will be twilight all life long.


The knives will already turn more lightly

because they will not find where to wound me.

Upright with black dews,

for you I will sing.


Let the sightless not seek me,

let the drowned not call me,

let those I flee not feel me!


To my solitude of reflections,

love,

only you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the voice hidden in a well of flame and the final solitude reserved for love.

title: Restlessness
text:
Where is my star kept,

my crystal of love?


The night denies me its dawn torso

and we go strange, detached,

never coinciding.


What for, if I am love to nothing,

am I love in what is unknown of me?


And this tenderness that girds my shoulders,

that awnings the gold of my heart,

what for, if I am searching for water

and know only the echo of the spring?
editorial_note: The translation preserves the inward questioning and the echo of the spring instead of water itself.

title: Adolescents
text:
Upon the eternal stone of the world so compact,

the weak, fresh trace of your naked body.

Everything is very hard and sour, it rebels, enemy,

and you rise so young and sure, so tender...


It is not true that flowers always fight silently.

They cry out their scent and die early,

while you, who are more, suffer twice as much as they do

and also die late, because you are already withering.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the contrast between the hard world, fragrant flowers, and the adolescent body's withering.

title: To Be Born to You Again...
text:
To be born to you again,

I want you to go ahead

of my steps over the earth,

which, though small, is very large.


Here you are accompanied

by my daily presence,

but orphaned of you

I would be, if you remained.


That is why I want you to walk,

little step by little step,

ahead and always ahead,

without hurry and without rest.


Thus, when I peer out

to the other side of here,

you will be prepared

to give birth to me again.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the reversal in which the beloved is asked to go first and rebirth the speaker.

title: Identification
text:
My eyes do not seek you over the immense earth!

you are my eyes dilating.

My eyes contain you; if you weep through them,

it is I who free myself from myself so that you may weep.


How you I am with myself, love; how you alienate me!

How mine your living and how mine your death,

coming to you from me, dying myself with you!


The weave of beating in a body that is not yours,

nor mine alone: a body of two beings

that fuse the unity of two who are already one.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Conde's intense identity exchange and the shared two-in-one body.

title: Rain in May
text:
How beautiful you are, sleepless one!

A sweet wind carries and shapes you

above gardens and statues.

Your body is Venus's on the shore,

eternally sea within the dawn.


Always come to me, be favorable to me.

The feast of leaves on their branches

is rendered to you by the slender dreamers

that rise in movable clusters.


I have not a single flower... Only my trunk

houses as fruit a bell.

Rain I contemplate, melancholy:

do not grow for me. I live flooded.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the sleepless rain/Venus image and the speaker already flooded.

title: Let Us Make a Pact, My Sea...
text:
Let us make a pact, my sea.

Confirm the pact for me entire.


When I go to the jungle of houses

and of pressing anonymous urgencies,

you must come, just as I see you,

as soon as my heart grows faint,

raising me before myself, archangelic immense blue,

bathing for me the hard world of my human surroundings.


And on nights of you, as soon as

their vast murmurs fall silent, pinewood and wind,

you must evoke me, you must listen to me,

saying to you:

I would like to be eternal, only to see you!




The Poems of Mar Menor, 1959
editorial_note: The translation keeps the pact with the sea and the closing wish for eternity only to see it.
